post.caption: Mae West's diamonds weren't all real. In her first film, Night After Night in 1932, a hat check girl admired her diamonds and West said goodness had nothing to do with it, dearie. One famous necklace in her collection mixed real diamonds with foil backed imitations. She left her jewelry to her companion, Charles Krauser, who had been a muscleman in her Las Vegas nightclub act. He kept it in a safe deposit box. West died in 1980 at age 87. Jeweler Neil Lane later bought a wide Art Deco diamond bracelet from the collection, and Catherine Zeta Jones wore it in the film Chicago.
